Toa Payoh

Toa Payoh

Toa Payoh 55

  1. Must see · Wok Noodles (Char Kway Teow, Hokkien Mee, Bak Chor Mee) · Toa Payoh

    Hai Nan Xing Zhou Beef Noodle

    Nearly 70 years of Hainanese beef noodles from S$5, newly awarded a Michelin Bib Gourmand — dry or soup, in a rich braise the whole hawker centre queues for.

    Kim Keat Palm Market & Food Centre, #01-06, Blk 22 Lorong 7 Toa Payoh, S310022

    Recommended by MICHELIN Guide — Bib Gourmand, Daniel Food Diary, Seth Lui, Eatbook.sg, Miss Tam Chiak

  2. Must see · Chinese, Dim Sum & Teochew · Toa Payoh

    Chey Sua Carrot Cake

    Michelin Bib Gourmand since 2016 — two sisters fry each plate of crispy-yet-spongy white carrot cake to order, drawing long queues at the freshly renovated (reopened Aug 2025) Toa Payoh West hawker centre.

    Toa Payoh West Market & Food Centre, #02-30, Blk 127 Lorong 1 Toa Payoh, S310127

    Recommended by MICHELIN Guide — Bib Gourmand, Seth Lui, Eatbook.sg, Daniel Food Diary

  3. Must see · Wok Noodles (Char Kway Teow, Hokkien Mee, Bak Chor Mee) · Toa Payoh

    Chef Kang's Noodle House

    A Michelin-starred Cantonese chef sells $5 wanton mee from a warehouse-canteen stall — HK-shipped springy noodles and charred char siew that earned a Michelin Bib Gourmand within a year of opening (still listed 2025/2026).

    Block A, Jackson Square, 11 Toa Payoh Lorong 3, S319579

    Recommended by MICHELIN Guide — Bib Gourmand, Daniel Food Diary, Miss Tam Chiak, Dr Leslie Tay (ieatishootipost)

  4. Must see · Toa Payoh

    Toa Payoh Dragon Playground

    Singapore's most iconic surviving 1979 mosaic 'dragon' playground, designed by HDB's Khor Ean Ghee — a terrazzo-tiled dragon head with a climbable ring body. One of only two dragon playgrounds left and a marquee stop on NHB's Toa Payoh Heritage Trail.

    Look for Open 24h, free

    Lorong 6 Toa Payoh (in front of Blk 28), Singapore

    Recommended by Roots.gov.sg (NHB), Wikipedia, Little Day Out

  5. Must see · Wok Noodles (Char Kway Teow, Hokkien Mee, Bak Chor Mee) · Toa Payoh

    Come Daily Fried Hokkien Prawn Mee

    Michelin-listed and running since 1968, Steven Ng reduces prawn stock right in the wok for one of Toa Payoh's most famous plates of Hokkien mee — a fixture of the reopened Toa Payoh West food centre.

    Toa Payoh West Market & Food Centre, #02-27, Blk 127 Lorong 1 Toa Payoh, S310127

    Recommended by MICHELIN Guide, Eatbook.sg, Daniel Food Diary

  6. Must see · Toa Payoh

    Lian Shan Shuang Lin Monastery

    Singapore's oldest Buddhist monastery — completed 1909 and gazetted a National Monument in 1980 — modelled on Fuzhou's Xi Chan Monastery, with the Hall of Celestial Kings and Mahavira Hall laid out in the classic cong lin ('layered forest') plan.

    Look for Free entry

    184 Jalan Toa Payoh, Singapore 319944

    Recommended by Roots.gov.sg (NHB), Wikipedia

  7. Must see · Toa Payoh

    United Temple (United Five Temples of Toa Payoh)

    Established 1974, the first temple in Singapore to house smaller constituent temples under one roof — five village temples (Chee Tian Keng, Shan Zu Yuan Fu De Ci, Tong Xing Gang, Zhao Ying Ci and others) that were displaced when Toa Payoh's kampongs were cleared pooled their devotees' funds to build here. A landmark on NHB's Toa Payoh Heritage Trail 'Of Faiths & Beliefs' route.

    Look for Free entry

    Lorong 6 Toa Payoh (near Blk 177/178), Singapore

    Recommended by Roots.gov.sg (NHB), The New Age Parents

  8. Must see · Wok Noodles (Char Kway Teow, Hokkien Mee, Bak Chor Mee) · Toa Payoh

    LiXin Teochew Fishball Noodles

    The original stall of Singapore's 58-year-old fishball dynasty (est. 1968), Michelin Bib Gourmand for four years running since 2022 — springy, umami yellowtail fishballs made fresh daily.

    Kim Keat Palm Market & Food Centre, #01-20, Blk 22 Lorong 7 Toa Payoh, S310022

    Recommended by MICHELIN Guide — Bib Gourmand, Daniel Food Diary

  9. Worth the detour · Malay & Nasi Padang · Toa Payoh

    Kedai Makan Muhajirin

    A beloved $1 nasi lemak that has held its price since 1987 to stay affordable for elderly regulars — cooking starts at 4am and 300-500 plates sell out by midday; covered by every major food outlet and YouTuber Ghib Ojisan.

    Blk 20 Toa Payoh Lorong 7 coffeeshop, S310020

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Eatbook.sg, Miss Tam Chiak, Mothership, AsiaOne, Ghib Ojisan (YouTube)

  10. Worth the detour · Chinese, Dim Sum & Teochew · Toa Payoh

    Old Long House Popiah

    A 3rd-generation popiah stall with roots to 1930, hand-rolling Hokkien-style popiah (no pork, no lard, no MSG) with house-fried sole-fish crisps — one of Singapore's most heritage popiah names.

    Kim Keat Palm Market & Food Centre, #01-03, Blk 22 Lorong 7 Toa Payoh, S310022

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Daniel Food Diary, Her World Singapore, Makansutra

  11. Worth the detour · Chendol, Kueh & Durian · Toa Payoh

    The Twisted Trio

    A hole-in-the-wall HDB cake cafe by three pastry-chef friends selling atas bakes from $3.50 — the chio Watermelon Rose cake (a nod to Black Star Pastry) and fudgy brownies among biscotti, pound cakes and cookies.

    Blk 85C Lorong 4 Toa Payoh, #01-385, S310085

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, Daniel Food Diary, Seth Lui, Miss Tam Chiak

  12. Worth the detour · Toa Payoh

    Toa Payoh Town Park & Look-Out Tower

    The 4.8-hectare 1970s town park that pioneered greenery in HDB new towns — landscaped ponds, rustic gazebos and the conserved 25 m space-age Look-Out Tower, a favourite 1970s-80s wedding-photo backdrop.

    Look for Open daily, free; tower not accessible

    Lorong 6 Toa Payoh (beside Toa Payoh HDB Hub), Singapore

    Recommended by Roots.gov.sg (NHB), Time Out Singapore, Little Day Out

  13. Worth the detour · Toa Payoh

    Toa Payoh Sensory Park

    Singapore's first sensory park (opened 2009), a 1.1-hectare garden by Surbana and Yoshisuke Miyake split into five zones for sight, smell, touch, sound and taste — with larger-than-life optical-illusion mirrors that reveal a hidden face, resonating steel 'drum' plates, a playground and a fragrant garden.

    Look for Open daily, free

    Lorong 5 / Lorong 6 Toa Payoh, Singapore

    Recommended by Little Day Out, The Smart Local, Wikipedia

  14. Worth the detour · Wok Noodles (Char Kway Teow, Hokkien Mee, Bak Chor Mee) · Toa Payoh

    Ru Ji Kitchen (Toa Payoh)

    The Toa Payoh outlet of Uncle David Ng's famed noodle stall, where bouncy yellowtail fishballs are hand-pounded on the spot (the Holland Drive original holds the Michelin Bib Gourmand).

    Blk 22 Lorong 7 Toa Payoh, #01-58, S310022

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Eatbook.sg, Daniel Food Diary

  15. Worth the detour · Chinese, Dim Sum & Teochew · Toa Payoh

    Teochew Handmade Pau

    A 30-plus-year heritage pau stall (est. 1993, three years on the Michelin Plate) hand-making Teochew-style buns with thick, not-too-sweet lotus paste — announced closure end-2025 but reopened June 2026 after public demand.

    Toa Payoh West Market & Food Centre, Blk 127 Lorong 1 Toa Payoh, S310127

    Recommended by Miss Tam Chiak, Daniel Food Diary, AsiaOne

  16. Worth the detour · Hawker & Zi Char · Toa Payoh

    Grandpa Homemade Cheung Fun

    A father-and-son team from Shenzhen mill their own rice flour on a stone grinder to make thicker, rustic cheung fun to order, tinted naturally with spinach and pink dragonfruit across 13 fillings — a standout of the reopened (Aug 2025) Toa Payoh West hawker centre.

    Toa Payoh West Market & Food Centre, #02-22, Blk 127 Lorong 1 Toa Payoh, S310127

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, Seth Lui, Daniel Food Diary

  17. Worth the detour · Chendol, Kueh & Durian · Toa Payoh

    Four Seasons Cendol

    Widely dubbed the best cendol in Singapore — and a favourite of ESM Goh Chok Tong, whose photos line the stall — with firmly-packed ice that stays solid, springy pandan jelly and gula melaka, plus Mao Shan Wang / D24 durian tops.

    Toa Payoh Lorong 8 Market & Food Centre, #01-07, Blk 210 Lorong 8 Toa Payoh, S310210

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, Seth Lui, Daniel Food Diary

  18. Worth the detour · Chinese, Dim Sum & Teochew · Toa Payoh

    Ah Chuan Fried Oyster Omelette

    A 50-year-old orh chien specialist (open ~3 hours a day) frying crisp-yet-chewy potato-starch batter with fluffy egg and juicy large Korean oysters, finished with crunchy parsley — a repeat pick on 'best oyster omelette' lists.

    Kim Keat Palm Market & Food Centre, #01-25, Blk 22 Lorong 7 Toa Payoh, S310022

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Johor Kaki (Tony Boey), Eatbook.sg

  19. Worth the detour · Wok Noodles (Char Kway Teow, Hokkien Mee, Bak Chor Mee) · Toa Payoh

    Cai Ji Fishball Noodle

    A 58-year cult favourite with arguably the longest queue in Palm Spring from 6am — springy mee pok tossed in a punchy chilli sauce with hand-made fishballs and meatballs; dry or soup.

    Toa Payoh Palm Spring Market, Blk 93 Lorong 4 Toa Payoh, S310093

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Miss Tam Chiak, Johor Kaki (Tony Boey)

  20. Worth the detour · Hawker & Zi Char · Toa Payoh

    Soon Heng Rojak

    A decades-old rojak stall by the HDB Hub food-court escalator with a permanent 20-30 minute queue — a generous mountain of youtiao, cucumber, pineapple, turnip and cuttlefish drowned in prawn-paste, torch-ginger and mounds of peanut.

    Gourmet Paradise Food Court, Toa Payoh HDB Hub, #B1-01, Blk 480 Lorong 6 Toa Payoh, S310480

    Recommended by HungryGoWhere, Eatbook.sg, Johor Kaki (Tony Boey)

  21. Worth the detour · Chinese, Dim Sum & Teochew · Toa Payoh

    Biang Biang Noodles Xi'an Famous Food

    A rare hawker source of Xi'an biang biang noodles — extra-wide belt noodles hand-stretched and slapped against the counter, tossed with braised pork, tomato-egg and chilli, plus rou jia mo (Chinese 'burger'); a hidden gem at Toa Payoh Central's Food Alley.

    Food Alley, 190 Lorong 6 Toa Payoh, #01-518, Toa Payoh Central, S310190

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, Seth Lui, Miss Tam Chiak

  22. Worth the detour · Toa Payoh

    Church of the Risen Christ

    Toa Payoh's first Catholic church (inaugurated 1971), a modernist landmark at the junction of Toa Payoh Central and Lorong 4 that has long offered Mass in English, Mandarin and Tamil — featured on the Toa Payoh Heritage Trail's 'Of Faiths & Beliefs' route.

    91 Toa Payoh Central, Singapore 319193

    Recommended by Roots.gov.sg (NHB), Wikipedia

  23. Worth the detour · Toa Payoh

    Block 53, The 'VIP Block'

    The Y-shaped 1967 HDB showpiece with a rooftop viewing gallery once used to survey the young new town from above. Queen Elizabeth II visited in 1972 (as did Princess Anne, Prince Philip and other dignitaries), earning it the 'VIP Block' name.

    Look for Rooftop gallery closed; view from ground level

    53 Lorong 5 Toa Payoh, Singapore 310053

    Recommended by Roots.gov.sg (NHB), Wikipedia

  24. Worth the detour · Toa Payoh

    Toa Payoh Heritage Trail

    NHB's self-guided trail through Singapore's second satellite town, linking 16-plus sites — from the Dragon Playground and Town Park to Shuang Lin Monastery — across two themed routes, 'Of Public Housing & Shared Spaces' and 'Of Faiths & Beliefs'.

    Look for Free; map downloadable on Roots.gov.sg

    Toa Payoh Central (trail starts near HDB Hub), Singapore

    Recommended by Roots.gov.sg (NHB), Little Day Out

  25. Worth the detour · Toa Payoh

    Sri Vairavimada Kaliamman Temple

    A Dravidian-style Hindu temple to the goddess Kaliamman, tracing to an 1860 shrine near Orchard Road and rebuilt at Toa Payoh in 1982 (consecrated 1986). Notable for founding Saraswathi Kindergarten, said to be Singapore's first pre-school, and a stop on the Toa Payoh Heritage Trail's 'Of Faiths & Beliefs' route.

    Look for Free entry

    2001 Lorong 8 Toa Payoh, Singapore 319259

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Roots.gov.sg (NHB)

  26. Worth the detour · Toa Payoh

    Toa Payoh Public Library

    Inaugurated 7 Feb 1974, the second public library of the 1970s branch-building drive and a civic anchor of the town — its Children's Section riffs on the iconic dragon playground with hexagonal mosaic-tile motifs. A pioneering heartland library documented in NLB's BiblioAsia.

    Look for Free; closed Mondays historically — check hours

    6 Toa Payoh Central, Singapore 319191

    Recommended by National Library Board, Wikipedia

  27. Worth the detour · Hainanese Chicken Rice · Toa Payoh

    Da Ji Hainanese Chicken Rice

    A cult chicken rice stall that swaps roast/poached chicken for addictively marinated crispy fried wings ($3.50) with a spicy chilli dip — famously long evening queues until sold out.

    Toa Payoh Lorong 5 Food Centre, #01-31, Blk 75 Lorong 5 Toa Payoh, S310075

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, Miss Tam Chiak

  28. Worth the detour · Wok Noodles (Char Kway Teow, Hokkien Mee, Bak Chor Mee) · Toa Payoh

    Lai Heng Mushroom Minced Meat Noodle

    A bak chor mee institution running since 1985 (relocated twice within Toa Payoh), still turning out a spicy dry mee kia and a standout lard-rich kway teow soup that Seth Lui rated after 24 years of visits.

    Blk 73 Toa Payoh Lorong 5, Toa Payoh

    Recommended by Seth Lui, HungryGoWhere

  29. Worth the detour · Chendol, Kueh & Durian · Toa Payoh

    Uggli Muffins

    UK-trained ex-engineer Anton Tan turned his family's zi char stall into a viral $1.20 muffin institution — deliberately misshapen buns with crunchy caramelised crusts; a long-queue hawker-dessert cult reopened after the 2025 renovation.

    Toa Payoh West Market & Food Centre, #02-34, Blk 127 Lorong 1 Toa Payoh, S310127

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Daniel Food Diary

  30. Worth the detour · Hawker & Zi Char · Toa Payoh

    Allauddin's Briyani (Toa Payoh Lor 8)

    The Toa Payoh outlet of the Tekka Centre briyani institution — a Michelin Plate / Michelin-recommended name whose fragrant $6 chicken, mutton and fish briyani draw a queue; the pull-apart rice and house sambal are the draw.

    Toa Payoh Lorong 8 Market & Food Centre, #01-79, Blk 210 Lorong 8 Toa Payoh, S310210

    Recommended by MICHELIN Guide, Daniel Food Diary

  31. Worth the detour · Hawker & Zi Char · Toa Payoh

    Yokozuna Stall

    An ex-hotel chef plates restaurant-grade Japanese food from a kopitiam beside the Lorong 8 hawker centre — the Tataki Salmon Roll ($6) and Butter Yaki Seabass Bento ($6.80) look far pricier than they cost; nothing on the menu tops $10.

    211 Lorong 8 Toa Payoh, #01-01, S310211

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, Seth Lui

  32. Worth the detour · Wok Noodles (Char Kway Teow, Hokkien Mee, Bak Chor Mee) · Toa Payoh

    Da Lao Fried White Kway Teow

    A one-man wok turning out Penang-style fried white kway teow with serious wok hei — clean, coated-not-greasy strands with fish cake, lap cheong and cockles from $4; the single-hand pace means a wait, and a long queue.

    Toa Payoh Lorong 8 Market & Food Centre, #01-23, Blk 210 Lorong 8 Toa Payoh, S310210

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Eatbook.sg

  33. Worth the detour · Wok Noodles (Char Kway Teow, Hokkien Mee, Bak Chor Mee) · Toa Payoh

    Song Kee Kway Teow Noodle Soup

    A 16-year evening-only stall (5pm–midnight) whose fishballs are pounded from scratch at 3am — bouncy, fresh yellowtail fishballs and fragrant fish dumplings over springy mee pok that fans call the best in Singapore.

    Toa Payoh Lorong 5 Food Centre, Blk 75 Lorong 5 Toa Payoh, S310075

    Recommended by Miss Tam Chiak, Daniel Food Diary

  34. Worth the detour · Chinese, Dim Sum & Teochew · Toa Payoh

    Palm Spring Kway Chap

    A second-generation kway chap running since 1967 and rated Singapore's best-rated kway chap — spice-forward braised innards, tau pok and silky rice sheets from 5.30pm, with snaking queues before it even opens.

    Toa Payoh Palm Spring Market, Blk 93 Lorong 4 Toa Payoh, S310093

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Johor Kaki (Tony Boey)

  35. Worth the detour · Indian & Roti Prata · Toa Payoh

    Rahmath Cheese Prata

    A Vista Market morning fixture drawing daily queues for crisp roti prata — plain to cheese-and-egg and sweet banana — then Indian-Muslim mee goreng, nasi goreng merah and tulang merah after 1.30pm; carries a Makansutra 'Divine' rating.

    Toa Payoh Vista Market, 74 Lorong 4 Toa Payoh, S310074

    Recommended by Miss Tam Chiak, Daniel Food Diary

  36. Worth the detour · Chendol, Kueh & Durian · Toa Payoh

    Creamier Handcrafted Ice Cream & Coffee

    The original heartland home of a beloved SG ice-cream name — handcrafted scoops like Earl Grey Lavender and Sea Salt Gula Melaka over freshly-pressed, crisp-outside pillowy Belgian waffles; the Toa Payoh dessert stop.

    Blk 128 Lorong 1 Toa Payoh, #01-829, S310128

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, The Honeycombers Singapore

  37. Deep cut · Toa Payoh

    Toa Payoh HDB Hub

    HDB's headquarters and the civic heart of Singapore's first fully HDB-built satellite town, home to relocated public sculptures — Ng Eng Teng's 'The Climb', Chong Fah Cheong's 'Mama's Precious One' and Ju Ming's 'Tai Chi Boxing' — plus a mall, library and hawker fare.

    480 Lorong 6 Toa Payoh, Singapore 310480

    Recommended by Housing & Development Board (heritage studies), Little Day Out

  38. Deep cut · Toa Payoh

    Toa Payoh Seu Teck Sean Tong

    A Chinese charitable temple established as an attap hut in 1942 and rebuilt 1959, enshrining the deity Song Da Feng and blending Buddhist, Taoist and Confucian rites. Its medical wing (opened 1967) still gives free Traditional Chinese Medicine consultations — a living community institution on the heritage trail.

    Look for Free entry; free TCM clinic

    15 Lorong 6 Toa Payoh (Kampong Hup Choon Hng site), Singapore

    Recommended by Roots.gov.sg (NHB), Toa Payoh Seu Teck Sean Tong (official)

  39. Deep cut · Toa Payoh

    Toa Payoh MRT Heritage Mural

    A station wall mural in SMRT's heritage-mural series telling Toa Payoh's story as the first town wholly designed and built by the HDB — co-created by James Suresh, better known as co-creator of the 'Mr Kiasu' comics. A quick, free public-art stop right at the interchange.

    Look for Free; inside paid transit area

    Toa Payoh MRT Station (NS19), 480 Lorong 6 Toa Payoh, Singapore

    Recommended by SMRT (official), SGTrains

  40. Deep cut · Toa Payoh

    SAFRA Toa Payoh

    The town's big community-and-sports clubhouse (open to the public, not just NSmen) with a leisure pool and lap lanes, bowling, badminton, tennis, gym, karaoke and F&B — the recreation hub that carries on locally while the adjacent old stadium and swimming complex are redeveloped into the Toa Payoh Integrated Development.

    Look for Facilities ticketed; entry free

    293 Toa Payoh Lorong 6, Singapore 319387

    Recommended by SAFRA (official), KidsGoWhere

  41. Deep cut · Chinese, Dim Sum & Teochew · Toa Payoh

    Hometaste Hakka Lei Cha

    Two sisters plate one of Singapore's most generous $5 thunder tea rice sets — less oil, less salt, no MSG — with the fragrant bitter-green tea broth poured over brown rice and crunchy toppings.

    Toa Payoh West Market & Food Centre, Blk 127 Lorong 1 Toa Payoh, S310127

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Daniel Food Diary

  42. Deep cut · Chendol, Kueh & Durian · Toa Payoh

    Pure Soya Bean

    Ex-Italian-restaurant cook Desheng makes beancurd from scratch daily with non-GMO soybeans — smooth, un-gritty tau huay you can dress with gula melaka, grass jelly or gingko.

    Toa Payoh West Market & Food Centre, Blk 127 Lorong 1 Toa Payoh, S310127

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Eatbook.sg

  43. Deep cut · Hawker & Zi Char · Toa Payoh

    Toa Payoh Scissors Cut Curry Rice

    Old-school Hainanese-style curry rice from S$2.80 — a heaped plate of chopped sides flooded in three different gravies (curry, braise, pork), a comfort-food fixture of Lorong 8.

    Toa Payoh Lorong 8 Market & Food Centre, 210 Lorong 8 Toa Payoh, S310210

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Eatbook.sg

  44. Deep cut · Chinese, Dim Sum & Teochew · Toa Payoh

    Uncle Kun's Delicacies (Kun Shu Food Stall)

    Ex-hotel HK chef Lam Kun serves restaurant-grade dim sum at hawker prices; his signature oblong scallop glutinous rice (S$4.80), packed with dried scallop, salted egg and lap cheong, isn't found elsewhere in Singapore.

    Toa Payoh Vista Market, Lorong 4 Toa Payoh

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Eatbook.sg

  45. Deep cut · Wok Noodles (Char Kway Teow, Hokkien Mee, Bak Chor Mee) · Toa Payoh

    Min Kee Tanjong Rhu Wanton Noodle

    A decades-old wanton mee that relocated from Tanjong Rhu, still selling a substantial $3.50 bowl of springy noodles with black-chilli option, soupy and fried wantons — a Kim Keat breakfast favourite.

    Kim Keat Palm Market & Food Centre, Blk 22 Lorong 7 Toa Payoh, S310022

    Recommended by Mothership, Daniel Food Diary

  46. Deep cut · Chendol, Kueh & Durian · Toa Payoh

    Hougang 6 Miles Famous Muah Chee

    Likely the last hawker hand-making this Teochew snack from scratch — Teo Yong Joo mills flour, roasts peanuts and pinches each soft, tender muah chee ball to order at the HDB Hub food court.

    Gourmet Paradise Food Court, Toa Payoh HDB Hub, Blk 480 Lorong 6 Toa Payoh, #B1-01, S310480

    Recommended by HungryGoWhere, Eatbook.sg

  47. Deep cut · Wok Noodles (Char Kway Teow, Hokkien Mee, Bak Chor Mee) · Toa Payoh

    Fried Fish Soup (Toa Payoh West)

    A no-frills stall doing a $3 bowl of fried fish ban mian — crispy fried fish slices, handmade noodles and a clean savoury broth — one of the value picks flagged across guides to the renovated Toa Payoh West food centre.

    Toa Payoh West Market & Food Centre, #02-24, Blk 127 Lorong 1 Toa Payoh, S310127

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Eatbook.sg

  48. Deep cut · Hawker & Zi Char · Toa Payoh

    Jia Le Man Fen Guo

    A 20-year veteran hand-tearing mee hoon kueh dough to order and ladling fish soup and porridge — old-school comfort noodles that regulars queue for at Toa Payoh West.

    Toa Payoh West Market & Food Centre, Blk 127 Lorong 1 Toa Payoh, S310127

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Eatbook.sg

  49. Deep cut · Hawker & Zi Char · Toa Payoh

    Seletar Sheng Mian Mee Hoon Kway

    Relocated from the demolished Seletar market, this snaking-queue stall hand-kneads, smacks and tears each piece of dough for uniquely textured sheng mian in a comforting pork-and-ikan-bilis broth from $3.

    Toa Payoh Lorong 8 Market & Food Centre, Blk 210 Lorong 8 Toa Payoh, S310210

    Recommended by SG Food on Foot, Johor Kaki (Tony Boey)

  50. Deep cut · Malay & Nasi Padang · Toa Payoh

    Fang Yuan Satay

    A 1966 satay stall now in its third generation, grilling well-marinated Chinese-style chicken and pork skewers over charcoal to order — beautifully charred sticks served with peanut sauce and fresh pineapple gravy.

    Toa Payoh Lorong 5 Food Centre, #01-25, Blk 75 Lorong 5 Toa Payoh, S310075

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Her World Singapore

  51. Deep cut · Hawker & Zi Char · Toa Payoh

    Economical Fried Bee Hoon & Noodle

    The stall with Kim Keat Palm's longest breakfast queue — wok-fried bee hoon and noodles with cabbage, best paired with a runny-yolk sunny-side-up egg; a heartland morning staple.

    Kim Keat Palm Market & Food Centre, Blk 22 Lorong 7 Toa Payoh, S310022

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, Daniel Food Diary

  52. Deep cut · Vietnamese · Toa Payoh

    2612 Little Vietnam Cuisine

    A husband-and-wife stall (she's Vietnamese) doing soul-comforting pho with broth simmered 8 hours on beef shank and shin, plus crisp fried spring rolls stuffed with pork, prawn and glass noodles — sauces imported from Vietnam, everything under $10.

    Blk 125 Lorong 1 Toa Payoh, #01-, S310125

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Miss Tam Chiak

  53. Deep cut · Cafés & Modern · Toa Payoh

    Niche Savoureuse

    An under-rated heartland cafe run by a France-trained baker — everything is handmade in-house, from crusty tiger bread and light not-too-sweet cakes to a Nyonya chendol waffle; a quaint wooden-front hideout beside Creamier.

    Blk 128 Lorong 1 Toa Payoh, #01-833, S310128

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Eatbook.sg

  54. Closed — kept for the record · Bak Kut Teh & Soups · Toa Payoh

    Hup Chong Hakka Yong Tau Foo — CLOSED

    A four-generation Hakka yong tau foo with roots to a 1952 pushcart, famous for handmade fried meatballs and fish paste — it closed for good on 28 Jan 2026 after 70-plus years amid falling footfall. Kept here as a flagged closure.

    Blk 203 Toa Payoh (final location; earlier Blk 116/124)

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Miss Tam Chiak, Eatbook.sg, AsiaOne, Mothership, Dr Leslie Tay (ieatishootipost)

  55. Closed — kept for the record · Wok Noodles (Char Kway Teow, Hokkien Mee, Bak Chor Mee) · Toa Payoh

    Kim Keat Hokkien Mee — CLOSED

    Once rated among Singapore's top-five Hokkien mee — served in a heat-retaining claypot with deep-fried crispy pork belly — this 10-year Toa Payoh favourite shuttered on 28 Feb 2026. Kept here as a flagged closure.

    Blk 92 Toa Payoh Lorong 4, #01-264, S310092

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, Daniel Food Diary, AsiaOne

14 sights and 41 places to eat in Toa Payoh, a town of Singapore, each traceable to the source that named it (Michelin, local news & vetted local/viral creators). Renders in soft pastel, light or dark.

How this guide was made

Web-searched & fact-checked

Every place is traceable to a credible source — Michelin, UNESCO, local news & magazines, and vetted local/viral creators — in data/sources.json. Coordinates are verified into data/geocodes.json and every place status-checked open. Yelp/TripAdvisor never count toward the two-source bar.

Cleo beta — every place is carried from the current live guide, with its sources. Map tiles: © OpenStreetMap contributors; Esri. All destinations.
